sections.content: Repository guidance separates control-plane, service, and sandbox responsibilities, preserves compatibility, protects sensitive and live paths, and requires evidence-backed validation. The referenced skills define VDD planning, Quick Dev TDD execution, and acceptance review as separate non-authorizing stages with explicit lifecycle ownership. ADRs establish immutable knowledge sources, hash-bound locator and publication workflows, degraded successor handling, persisted acceptance evidence, and v2 skill-input selection with complete coverage and retention controls.
sections.title: Governance and lifecycle

sections.content: The toolchain repair plan defines slices W0 through W6 for typed source selection, transport, coverage, knowledge gates, immutable generations, retention, and end-to-end migration. Contracts require hidden-state-free execution, shell-disabled structured commands, hash-bound identities, declared write sets, staged RED/GREEN/REFACTOR evidence, and empty authorizations. Validators check canonical identities, authority and validator roots, required artifacts, lifecycle projections, plan readiness, and terminal implementation-complete predicates.
sections.title: Execution plan and validation

sections.content: The supplied tests cover degraded knowledge continuation, missing-page rejection, immutable current-pointer behavior, approval-gated retention, separate selection and content identities, transport resume identity, and end-to-end typed selection. Acceptance evidence is persisted and replayable, requires matching registries, contracts, receipts, and context bindings, and keeps publication, lifecycle transitions, bootstrap review, release, and commit outside these inputs.
